comparison.verdict: The adapter beats the pattern baseline by 0.489 strict F1. Unlike urgency, the PII adapter clearly earns its place.

notes: Written to be a fair baseline, not a strawman: patterns are ordered most-specific-first, closed classes (TITLE/GENDER/SEX) use lexicons, and the design is documented with what it can and cannot reach before it was run.

Structural ceiling is ~58% recall (the pattern- and lexicon-reachable share of spans). Measured recall is 0.307 — barely half of that, because the numeric labels are mutually ambiguous as character sequences. A pattern precise enough for one costs recall on another.
EMAIL at 0.995 and ZIPCODE at 0.166 are the two ends of the same phenomenon: a shape nothing else shares versus five digits that look like everything else.
The four largest name-like labels (GIVENNAME, SURNAME, CITY, STREET — 33% of spans) are not attempted at all; they need NER. A spaCy baseline would raise this number and has not been run.

Fair-comparison caveat: the adapter's 0.9190 was measured on an A10 via generation; this baseline runs locally and is deterministic. Both use the identical 300-document golden set and the same scorer.
Kept as the pattern-only component. The headline baseline is now regex+spaCy at 0.5006 strict; this file isolates how much of that comes from patterns alone.
